vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clipboard-memory
Version: 1.1.1

The skill bundle provides an interface for an AI agent to query and export data from a local SQLite archive of the macOS clipboard history via the 'clipmem' utility. While the tool is presented as a productivity aid for recalling past snippets, providing an agent with programmatic access to a searchable history of clipboard states (including text, URLs, and binary data) represents a high-risk capability. Clipboards frequently contain sensitive information such as passwords, API keys, and PII, making this a primary target for credential harvesting. The bundle includes a diagnostic script (scripts/check-setup.sh) and detailed documentation (SKILL.md, references/commands.md) but lacks explicit evidence of data exfiltration or intentional malice, fitting the criteria for a high-risk 'suspicious' classification.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and runtime instructions match its stated purpose (using the local clipmem tool to recall clipboard history on macOS); nothing requests unrelated credentials or hidden network exfiltration, but the tool does access all clipboard contents (including sensitive data) and installs/relies on a background watcher, so review the upstream package before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the declared requirements: the skill needs the clipmem binary and runs only macOS-local commands to read a local SQLite clipboard archive. The brew formula and optional cargo package are appropriate for delivering the clipmem binary.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run only clipmem subcommands, a local health-check script, and to read/write local files (database at ~/Library/Application Support/clipmem/clipmem.sqlite3 and exported files). There are no instructions to contact external endpoints or read unrelated system credentials. Note: the agent will be able to access all clipboard history (text, images, PDFs, file-URLs), which is expected but sensitive.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Install uses a Homebrew formula (tristanmanchester/tap/clipmem) and references cargo as an alternate. This is reasonable but the brew tap is a third-party tap (not the macOS default core). Verify the upstream tap/package source and checksums before installing if you require vetted code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No secrets or unrelated environment variables are required. The references mention CLIPMEM_OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE and HOME for path resolution, which are reasonable optional environment hooks and not required credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal agent invocation. The tool expects a persistent watcher daemon (LaunchAgent io.openclaw.clipmem.watch) to capture clipboard events; that implies a background process storing clipboard history on disk. This persistent capture is coherent with the skill's purpose but has privacy implications the user should be aware of.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it queries a local clipmem archive to recover clipboard history. Before installing or enabling it, review the clipmem Homebrew tap/source (tristanmanchester/tap) to ensure you trust the release; confirm the binary will be installed from a source you trust. Be aware that clipmem maintains a local archive and (if the watcher/LaunchAgent is enabled) continually records clipboard contents — that can include passwords, 2FA codes, private keys, and other sensitive data. If you accept that privacy tradeoff, ensure the DB file permissions and location are acceptable, and use the included scripts (scripts/check-setup.sh and clipmem doctor) to validate installation and health. If you do not want persistent clipboard capture, do not enable or install the watcher/LaunchAgent.
